# A measured joule becomes warm water
# Expectation: 10 kJ into 100 g water should raise temperature roughly 24 K, without mass loss below boiling.
register lv3
add v1 water 100g
heat v1 10kJ
inspect v1
measure v1 thermometer
measure v1 balance

# Undo a thermal pulse
# Expectation: Heating then removing the same 10 kJ should return 100 g water close to its initial temperature and mass.
register lv3
add v1 water 100g
heat v1 10kJ
cool v1 10kJ
inspect v1

# Mix unequal hot and cold portions
# Expectation: 75 g at 20 C plus 25 g at 80 C should equilibrate near 35 C; mass should be 100 g.
register lv3
add v1 water 75g @ 20C
add v1 water 25g @ 80C
inspect v1

# A double dose is not a double temperature rise
# Expectation: Equal 10 kJ pulses into 100 g and 200 g water should produce approximately 2:1 temperature rises.
register lv3
add v1 water 100g
new
add v2 water 200g
heat v1 10kJ
heat v2 10kJ
inspect

# Latent heat intercepts the cooling pulse
# Expectation: Removing 20 kJ from 100 g water initially at 5 C should give an ice/water mixture near 0 C, not liquid at -43 C.
register lv3
add v1 water 100g @ 5C
cool v1 20kJ
inspect v1
measure v1 ph

# Boiling spends energy on disappearing liquid
# Expectation: 40 kJ into 100 g water at 95 C should approach 100 C and evaporate roughly 17 g rather than heat all liquid to 190 C.
register lv3
add v1 water 100g @ 95C
heat v1 40kJ
inspect v1
measure v1 ph

# Heat dilution cannot invent energy
# Expectation: Mixing two equal water portions at 60 C should keep them near 60 C, not reset the second dose to room temperature.
register lv3
add v1 water 50g @ 60C
add v1 water 50g @ 60C
inspect v1

# A tenfold acid dilution
# Expectation: Diluting 0.001 mol HCl in 100 mL water with another 900 mL should raise pH by about one unit (roughly 2 to 3).
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 HCl 0.001mol
measure v1 ph
dilute v1 900mL
measure v1 ph
inspect v1

# Acid/base cancellation and overshoot
# Expectation: 0.001 mol HCl followed by equal NaOH should reach near-neutral pH; another 0.001 mol NaOH should make it alkaline.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 HCl 0.001mol
add v1 NaOH 0.001mol
measure v1 ph
add v1 NaOH 0.001mol
measure v1 ph
inspect v1

# Weak acid versus strong acid
# Expectation: Equal 0.001 mol doses in 100 mL should give acetic acid a higher pH than HCl, by at least one unit.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL

new
add v2 water 100mL

measure v1 ph
measure v2 ph
inspect

register lv3

measure v1 ph
inspect v1

# Expectation: A half-neutralised acetate buffer should change pH far less than plain water after the same 0.0001 mol HCl pulse.

register lv3
